newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech Tatra has 625 mln Czech crown 96 loss - paper.
newsitem.headline: Czech Tatra has 625 mln Czech crown 96 loss - paper.

text.p: Auditors at troubled Czech truck maker Tatra a.s., controlled by engineering concern Skoda a.s., have confirmed the firm posted a 625 million crown ($18.4 million) loss in 1996, the economic daily Hospodarske Noviny reported on Wednesday.

The loss -- which brings Tatra's losses for the past five years to 4.3 billion crowns -- is the firm's best result in five years. Tatra lost 775 million crowns in 1995. Its worst result was in 1993 when it posted a 2.26 billion crown loss.
Company officials were not immediately for comment.
The paper quoted Skoda spokesman Jaroslav Hudec as saying one major problem Tatra faces is a heavy debt burden, mainly 2.8 billion crowns to Komercni Banka.
He added that since Komercni has granted the firm a respite from interest and principal payments on the debt in the first half of 1997, Tatra posted a 137 million crown profit for the period.
Tatra officials have said the company plans to make 3,200 trucks this year, and swing to a 70 million crown net profit.
Last year Skoda a.s. acquired a controlling stake in the debt-ridden firm and made it a part of its growing engineering group, which also includes another truck maker, Skoda LIAZ a.s..

Tatra, during its peak production years, once produced up to 15,000 heavy-duty trucks per year, but production fell sharply after the 1989 end of communism. Tatra also makes a small number of luxury limousines and light utility vehicles.
Gerald Greenwald, a former Chrysler vice president and a team of American auto executives attempted to rescue the firm in 1993. Tatra saw its worst result in 1993, posting a 2.26 billion crown loss.
The Americans left when Greenwald took over as the head of United Airlines parent UAL Corp. in 1994.
Skoda has revealed a plan to start production of Detroit Diesel Corp engines at Tatra's plant.
